timeline_list.title: A Primeira Exibição
timeline_list.description: Auguste (1862-1954) e Louis (1864-1948) Lumière exibem 10 curtas-metragens em Paris para um público pagante, entre eles, A saída dos operários da fábrica Lumière.

image.content_description: Foto de Auguste e Louis Lumière

timeline_list.title: The world's first film company
timeline_list.description: Comptoir Général de Photographie, under the name Gaumont, became the world's first film company – and the oldest one still in operation. It was here that Alice Guy Blaché started out as a secretary, before becoming one of the most important directors in cinema.

image.content_description: Photo with the logo of the Comptoir Général de Photographie company

timeline_list.title: A Controversial Kiss
timeline_list.description: Thomas Edison, the father of the kinetoscope, releases what may be the first major controversy in film history, The Kiss (1896), directed by William Heise, the first film to show a kiss on the big screen.

image.content_description: Scene from The Kiss, with the two main characters kissing.

timeline_list.title: The Beginning of Narrative
timeline_list.description: In 1896, Alice Guy Blaché releases the world's first non-fiction film. La Fée aux choux (The Cabbage-Patch Fairy, 1896), just one minute long, was written, produced and directed by her. Alice Guy's film features sets, cuts, special effects and a narrative, however brief.

image.content_description: Profile photo of director Alice Guy Blaché, next to a camera.

timeline_list.title: Phantom Ride
timeline_list.description: George Albert Smith filmed what came to be known as a "phantom ride" in his film The Kiss in the Tunnel (1899). It was a new visual experience for audiences, achieved by placing the camera on the front of a moving train, as if it were a ghostly eye gliding through the air.

image.content_description: Photo of George Albert Smith during the shooting of his film, sitting on the front of a train, attempting the Phantom Ride.

timeline_list.title: Narrative Complexity
timeline_list.description: A few years after Alice's film was released, the film Attack on a China Mission - Bluejackets to the Rescue (1900) is shown at Hove Town Hall, in the county of Sussex. A watershed moment for cinema, James Williamson (1855-1933) created one of the most complex narratives of its time.

image.content_description: Scene from Attack on a China Mission, with the soldiers running out of the burning building.

timeline_list.title: A New Standard
timeline_list.description: In Le Voyage dans la Lune (A Trip to the Moon, 1902), Georges Méliès sets a new standard for production and special effects costs.

image.content_description: Scene from A Trip to the Moon, in which a moon with a human face is hit in the right eye by a rocket.

timeline_list.title: Technical Evolution
timeline_list.description: The average length of a film reel grows from 15 to 183 meters, allowing more time to develop a narrative.

image.content_description: Photo of a film reel.

timeline_list.title: Close-up
timeline_list.description: The Sick Kitten (1903), a remake of The Little Doctor (1901), both by George Albert Smith, is released. In it, we first see a room, two children and a cat: the main shot. Then Smith cuts to a close-up of the cat being given a spoonful of medicine. This is considered the first use of a close-up that doesn't involve characters looking through something.

image.content_description: Close-up of a cat sitting on a woman's lap.

timeline_list.title: Continuidade nas telas
timeline_list.description: Life of an American Fireman (A vida de um bombeiro americano, 1903), de Edwin Porter é lançado. Na sequência onde o bombeiro chega à casa pegando fogo, Edwin corta para um quarto dentro da casa, mostrando o resgate de uma mulher pelo bombeiro e, depois, corta para um plano exterior da mãe na rua. Para muitos historiadores, esse foi o primeiro exemplo de edição de continuidade.

image.content_description: Cena do filme A vida de um bombeiro americano, com o bombeiro subindo uma escada.

timeline_list.title: O Primeiro longa-metragem
timeline_list.description: The story of the Kelly Gang (1906), de Charlie Tait é lançado na Austrália, possuindo mais de uma hora de duração. Sua bobina possuía mais de 1200 metros, se tornando o primeiro longa-metragem da história do cinema.

image.content_description: cena do filme The story of the Kelly Gang, com um homem usando uma mascara de ferro.

timeline_list.title: O começo de Hollywood
timeline_list.description: D.W. Griffith dirige o curta-metragem de 17 minutos In Old California (Na velha Califórnia, 1910), a primeira película filmada em Hollywood.

image.content_description: Foto do terreno onde futuramente seria Hollywood.

timeline_list.title: Famous Players Film Company
timeline_list.description: Fundada por Adolph Zukor, Famous Players Film Company se torna a primeira produtora americana a se dedicar exclusivamente à produção de longas-metragens.

image.content_description: Foto do logo da produtora Famous Players Film Company.

timeline_list.title: A Era Vampe
timeline_list.description: Clara Pontoppidan interpreta a primeira vampe do cinema no influente melodrama erótico Vampyrdanserinden (BR: O vampiro dançarino, 1912).

image.content_description: Foto de Clara Pontoppidan dançando em cena durante o filme O vampiro dançarino.

timeline_list.title: Superproduções
timeline_list.description: Cabiria (1914) custa mais de 1 milhão de liras para ser realizado e se torna o filme mais caro de sua época.

image.content_description: Cena do filme Cabiria, com uma multidão em volta de um antigo monumento.

timeline_list.title: The "Tramp"
timeline_list.description: O "vagabundo" de Chaplin estreia nas telas em Kid Auto Races at Venice (BR: Corrida de automóveis para meninos, 1914).

image.content_description: Photo of Charlie Chaplin's face.

timeline_list.title: A controversial milestone
timeline_list.description: The Birth of a Nation (1915), at 190 minutes, breaks the record for the longest film ever made. At the same time, the film revives interest in the Ku Klux Klan, which by then had all but disappeared. A year after its release, D. W. Griffith responds to accusations of prejudice by making the epic Intolerance: Love's Struggle Throughout the Ages (1916).

image.content_description: Scene from The Birth of a Nation, with an African American man being captured by members of the Ku Klux Klan.

timeline_list.title: The first adult film in cinema
timeline_list.description: A Free Ride (1915) is released and is considered the first classic pornographic film, alongside El Satario (1907) in Argentina and Am Abend (1910) in Germany. The 9-minute film follows a driver who gives a ride to two women by the side of the road, and further along they have sex. Researchers say the crew probably made an effort to keep the cast unidentifiable, since the actor wore a large fake mustache and a hat, and their identities were left anonymous in the credits. The director also remained anonymous, using the pseudonym A Wise Guy, and the only name revealed was that of Will B. Hard, the cinematographer.

image.content_description: Scene from A Free Ride, with a car driving alongside some women.

timeline_list.title: Cinema in the classroom
timeline_list.description: Soviet cinema is nationalized and the world's first film school, the All-Union State Institute of Cinematography, is founded in Moscow

image.content_description: Photo of the State Institute of Cinematography logo.

timeline_list.title: German Expressionism
timeline_list.description: Das Cabinet des Dr. Caligari (The Cabinet of Dr. Caligari, 1920), a disturbing classic of so-called German Expressionism, reflects its author's experiences in World War I. Essential to the development of the imagination, this film introduced many of the key elements of horror cinema.

image.content_description: Scene from The Cabinet of Dr. Caligari, with an old man looking off in one direction, his shadow cast on the wall.

timeline_list.title: Swashbuckler
timeline_list.description: Fred Niblo releases The Mark of Zorro (1920), marking the start of a new film genre: the swashbuckler. Zorro was the brainchild of Douglas Fairbanks, who produced and starred in the film.

image.content_description: Profile photo of the character Zorro.

timeline_list.title: A Symphony of Horror
timeline_list.description: F.W. Murnau releases Nosferatu (1922), an unauthorized adaptation of Bram Stoker's Dracula, which was nearly destroyed because of a lawsuit.

image.content_description: Scene from Nosferatu, with the Vampire looking straight at the screen.

timeline_list.title: Cinema's first idol
timeline_list.description: Rodolfo Valentino rises to stardom in The Four Horsemen of the Apocalypse (1921). That same year, he stars in The Sheik (1921), and women faint during screenings. Thanks to his exotic charm, he became Hollywood's first male sex symbol.

image.content_description: Profile photo of the actor Rodolfo Valentino.

timeline_list.title: One of the three kings of comedy
timeline_list.description: Safety Last! (1923) is released, starring Harold Lloyd, considered one of the three kings of silent comedy, alongside Charlie Chaplin and Buster Keaton. This film contains one of the most iconic moments of silent film, in which Lloyd finds himself hanging from the hands of a clock high up on a building.

image.content_description: Scene from Safety Last!, with the character The Boy hanging from the hand of a giant clock.

timeline_list.title: The Walt Disney Company is born
timeline_list.description: In early 1923, in Kansas City, Missouri, animator Walt Disney created a short film titled Alice's Wonderland, featuring child actress Virginia Davis interacting with animated characters. In 1923, after the bankruptcy of his first company, Laugh-O-Gram Films, Walt Disney moved to Hollywood to join his brother, Roy O. Disney. Film distributor Margaret J. Winkler, of M. J. Winkler Productions, contacted Disney with plans to distribute a series of Alice Comedies, purchased for 1,500 dollars per reel, with Walt Disney as a production partner. That same year, Walt and Roy Disney founded the Disney Brothers Animation Studios. Other animated films followed Alice. In January 1926, with the completion of the Disney studio's expansion on Hyperion Street, the studio's name was changed to Walt Disney Studios.

image.content_description: Scene from Alice's Wonderland, with the character Alice on top of an animated elephant, surrounded by several other animals.

timeline_list.title: The most profitable of its Era
timeline_list.description: The Big Parade (1925), by King Vidor, is released and grosses 22 million dollars at the box office worldwide, becoming the most successful silent film of all time.

image.content_description: Scene from The Big Parade, with the character Melisande kissing James on the cheek.

timeline_list.title: The Gold Rush
timeline_list.description: Chaplin releases The Gold Rush (1925), which becomes one of his most iconic and successful films. It is one of the highest-grossing films of the silent era.

image.content_description: Scene from The Gold Rush, with the Tramp character doing a dance with bread rolls stuck on forks.

timeline_list.title: Eisenstein
timeline_list.description: Sergei Eisenstein, considered one of the greatest and most important directors of all time, makes his first feature film: Стачка (Strike, 1925) is released on April 28, followed by Броненосец Потёмкин (Battleship Potemkin, 1925) on December 24.

image.content_description: Profile photo of director Sergei Eisenstein.

timeline_list.title: Technicolor
timeline_list.description: The Black Pirate (1926) is the first film made entirely in the two-color Technicolor process, an extremely expensive process at the time.

image.content_description: Profile photo of the character Jamie, in The Black Pirate.

timeline_list.title: A silent comedy classic
timeline_list.description: Buster Keaton completes The General (1926). A critical failure at the time, the film would later be rediscovered and hailed as one of the finest works of the silent era.

image.content_description: Scene from The General, with Buster Keaton on top of a locomotive.

timeline_list.title: Coming of age
timeline_list.description: At UFA, F. W. Murnau makes Faust – Eine deutsche Volkssage (Faust, 1926), a visual spectacle. The avant-garde Kurutta ippêji (A Page of Madness, 1926), by Teinosuke Kinugasa, demonstrates the maturity of Japanese silent film.

image.content_description: Scene from A Page of Madness, with two characters wearing masks.

timeline_list.title: "It Girl"
timeline_list.description: The shopgirl played by Clara Bow wins over her wealthy boss in It, whose title refers to the quality defined by screenwriter Elinor Glyn. Thanks to this film, Clara Bow became one of the screen's first sex symbols.

image.content_description: Photo of the face of the character Betty, played by actress Clara Bow.

timeline_list.title: A science fiction pioneer
timeline_list.description: Metropolis (1927), by Fritz Lang, is one of the first science fiction feature films. It is a dystopia set in a technologically advanced future.

image.content_description: Scene from Metropolis, with the robot standing in an empty room.

timeline_list.title: Surrealism
timeline_list.description: One of the greatest classics of surrealist cinema, Un chien andalou (1929), by Luis Buñuel, written by Buñuel himself and Salvador Dalí, premieres in Paris. The film wins over audiences and runs for eight months.

image.content_description: Scene from Un Chien Andalou, with a barber about to slice the eye of a woman staring fixedly at the screen.

timeline_list.title: A new Era
timeline_list.description: The silent film era comes to an end with the release of The Jazz Singer (1927), the first feature-length talkie shown on a large scale.

image.content_description: Scene from The Jazz Singer, with a character singing a song to a woman at the piano.

timeline_list.title: The Oscars
timeline_list.description: The first Academy Awards ceremony is held at the Hollywood Hotel in Los Angeles.

image.content_description: Photo of the first Oscars night, in a banquet hall.

timeline_list.title: Looney Tunes
timeline_list.description: Warner Bros. releases Looney Tunes cartoons in theaters. These short films predate Bugs Bunny, featuring the characters Bosko and Buddy instead.
